description:
IronPDF helps C# Software Engineers to create, edit and extract PDF content in .NET projects.

# C# HTML to PDF for .NET 10, .NET 9, .NET 8, .NET 7, .NET 6, .NET 5, Core, Standard, and Framework
# Work with PDFs in C# using HTML, MVC, ASPX, and images
# Generate, Edit, Read and Secure PDF Documents

Generate PDFs with Pixel Perfect Chrome HTML to PDF Rendering:
The Iron PDF library takes the frustration out of generating PDF documents by not relying on proprietary APIs. “Html-To-Pdf” renders pixel-perfect PDFs from open standard document types: HTML, JS, CSS, JPG, PNG, GIF, and SVG. In short, it uses the skills that developers already possess.

Fully Supports:
* .NET 10, .NET 9, .NET 8, .NET 7, .NET 6, .NET 5, Framework, Core, and Standard
* Windows, MacOS, Linux, Azure, Docker and AWS

For code examples, tutorials and documentation visit:
https://ironpdf.com/
releaseNotes:
Features
- Added opt-in bitonal (1-bit CCITT Group 4) image compression through AdvancedCompressionOptions for smaller and sharper scanned PDFs
- Added support for digitally signing an existing named signature field using PdfSignature.SignatureFieldName
- Added configurable Table of Contents titles and optional title entries through ChromePdfRenderOptions

Enhancements
- Improved tagged PDF handling when merging, importing, or securing PDFs; PDF/UA structure, document language, and accessibility metadata are now preserved for copied content

Bug Fixes
- Fixed an issue where RenderHtmlAsPdfUA could incorrectly mark a wrapped paragraph and following content as artifacts, causing meaningful text to be hidden from assistive technologies
- Fixed an issue where converting PDFs containing emoji or other transparent content to PDF/A-1 could retain unsupported transparency and fail PDF/A-1b validation
- Fixed an issue where PDF/UA output could lose the required PDF/UA identification metadata in XMP
- Fixed an issue where PDF/UA conversion could cause images to disappear after a page was resized
- Fixed an issue where saving merged documents as PDF/UA could produce content that strict PDF readers could not decode
- Fixed an issue where signing PDFs could create duplicate AcroForm signature field names; affected signatures are now reported with a warning during verification
- Fixed an issue affecting PDF processing on macOS Apple Silicon deployments
- Fixed an issue where a failed PdfDocument constructor could cause an unrelated open document to be closed
- Fixed intermittent crashes when PDF documents were accessed concurrently

Breaking Changes
- PdfDocument now supports adding one digital signature at a time; attempting to add a second signature to the same document throws an exception. To add multiple signatures, sign and save the document, reopen it, and then add the next signature

Updates
- Updated internal dependencies
